John Harbaugh delivered another big shakeup at running back on Tuesday..

The Giants released Najee Harris, just two days after Harbaugh benched Cam Skattebo and Harris appeared to be in line for the starting role.

Harris was the first running back in the game but he received just four carries for 2 yards in the Giants’ 34-27 loss to the Saints.

After the game, Harris bizarrely complained about his role, telling reporters that he needed more reps to get into the flow of a game.

“It’s hard to get into a rhythm with one or two runs,” Harris told reporters.

With Harris off the roster, the Giants are left with Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy Jr., and Devin Singletary in their backfield.

“Nobody has really taken the bull by the horns,” Harbaugh explained after the loss.

More to come on this breaking news story.
news.content: بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. جان هاربا در روز سه‌شنبه یک تغییر بزرگ دیگر در دویدن انجام داد. غول‌ها ناجی هریس را آزاد کردند، تنها دو روز پس از اینکه هاربا، کم اسکاتبو را نیمکت نشین کرد و به نظر می‌رسید که هریس برای نقش اصلی در صف قرار دارد. هریس اولین دونده در بازی بود، اما او تنها چهار بار در ازای 2 یارد به از دست دادن Giants در 3-4 دریافت کرد. پس از بازی، هریس به طرز عجیبی از نقش خود شکایت کرد و به خبرنگاران گفت که برای وارد شدن به جریان بازی به تکرارهای بیشتری نیاز دارد. هریس به خبرنگاران گفت: "در یک یا دو دویدن سخت است." با حذف هریس از فهرست، جاینت ها با اسکاتبو، تایرون تریسی جونیور باقی مانده اند، و دیوین واقعاً از بول فیلد عقب مانده است. هاربا پس از باخت توضیح داد. بیشتر در مورد این خبر فوری آمده است.

Ukrainian tennis pro Elina Svitolina explained that her decision to end her and Gaël Monfil’s marriage came down to more than Russia’s war in her native country.

The pair announced they were ending their marriage of five years in a joint Instagram post Monday, in which Svitolina, 32, shared she lost herself in the ongoing war and “with time, I came to understand that I need to find my way back to myself and that I cannot do that within our marriage.”

In another statement Tuesday, Svitolina further “clarified” her decision — and she explained that the 40-year-old Frenchman retired earlier than expected due to their divorce.

“I just want to clarify my previous post a little, because I realized that not everyone, especially my international audience, fully understood what I was trying to say,” Svitolina, who is ranked world No. 6, wrote.

“In that post, I shared only one of the reasons that influenced my decision and made me reflect on my life and my future. But the truth is, there’s so much more to it, and it was never just about one thing.

“When you’ve been living through the reality of war for more than 4.5 years, experiencing so many different situations, emotions, and difficult moments, you naturally start seeing life differently. Your perspective changes, your values and priorities shift, and you begin to understand what you truly want out of life.”

Svitolina and Monfils, who got married in Switzerland in July 2021, share a daughter named, Skaï, born in October 2022.

“At some point, I simply realized that I didn’t want to keep living a life where I wasn’t truly happy,” she said. “And believe me, coming to this decision was anything but easy. I love and respect my husband very much. And I will always love and appreciate him for the person he is. That’s exactly why it was so important for me to be honest, both with him and with myself.

“It’s not always possible to explain everything behind such personal and difficult decisions in a single post. And honestly, some things are simply too personal to share publicly. That was and is my view on announcing the end of our marriage but as some of you saw, Gael’s career ended abruptly after he made the decision to stop based on our situation. Unfortunately he had many accusations thrown at him and he didn’t deserve that, so we jointly released a statement.

“I just hope this helps you understand a little better what I was trying to say but please be kind and understanding, this is incredibly tough for us both right now 💔”.

Monfils — who previously announced last year that he would retire after a 22-year career at the Paris Masters in November — was registered as retired by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) on Oct. 5.

The 13-time ATP Tour singles champion withdrew from a wild card spot at the ATP 250 event in Lyon on Monday for “personal reasons,” the tournament said.

Monfils played his last professional match Sept. 3, losing in the second round of the US Open to Learner Tien (6–3, 6–4, 6–3).

The two reached the US Open mixed doubles semi-finals together in August.

Svitolina is the midst of a stellar 2026 campaign.

پوشش های بیشتری از ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. الینا سویتولینا، تنیس باز اوکراینی توضیح داد که تصمیم او برای پایان دادن به ازدواج او و گائل مونفیل بیشتر از جنگ روسیه در کشور مادری اش بوده است. این دو روز دوشنبه در پست مشترک اینستاگرامی خود اعلام کردند که به ازدواج پنج ساله خود پایان می دهند، که در آن سویتولینا، 32 ساله، خود را در جنگ جاری از دست داده است و "با گذشت زمان، فهمیدم که باید راه خود را پیدا کنم و نمی توانم این کار را در ازدواجمان انجام دهم." سویتولینا در بیانیه دیگری در روز سه شنبه تصمیم خود را "روشن" کرد - و او توضیح داد که این مرد فرانسوی 40 ساله به دلیل طلاق آنها زودتر از حد انتظار بازنشسته شد. "من فقط می خواهم کمی پست قبلی خود را توضیح دهم، زیرا متوجه شدم که همه، به ویژه مخاطبان بین المللی من، به طور کامل متوجه آنچه می خواستم بگویم، نبودند." در آن پست، من تنها یکی از دلایلی را به اشتراک گذاشتم که بر تصمیمم تأثیر گذاشت و باعث شد به زندگی و آینده‌ام فکر کنم. اما حقیقت این است که چیزهای بسیار بیشتری در آن وجود دارد، و هرگز فقط یک چیز نبود. «وقتی بیش از 4.5 سال است که در واقعیت جنگ زندگی می‌کنید، موقعیت‌های مختلف، احساسات و لحظات سخت را تجربه می‌کنید، به طور طبیعی شروع به دیدن زندگی متفاوت می‌کنید. دیدگاه شما تغییر می‌کند، ارزش‌ها و اولویت‌های شما تغییر می‌کند و شروع می‌کنید به درک آنچه واقعاً از زندگی می‌خواهید.»

Sam Altman on Tuesday won the dismissal of a civil lawsuit filed by his sister accusing the OpenAI co-founder and chief executive of repeated sexual abuse more than two decades ago, an accusation he denies.

In dismissing Annie Altman’s lawsuit, US District Judge Zachary Bluestone wrote that she had refused to appear for an independent medical examination despite warnings that failure to do so would result in the case’s dismissal.

Laura Politi, a lawyer for Annie Altman, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Santos Perez, a lawyer who previously represented Annie Altman in the case but withdrew this month, said in a statement, “I am no longer authorized to comment on this case but I continue to believe in Annie.”

Lawyers for Sam Altman did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Sam Altman became a face of the artificial intelligence boom after the chatbot ChatGPT was released in 2022.

Annie Altman brought her lawsuit in St. Louis federal court in January 2025.

She accused her brother of sexually abusing and raping her between 1997 and 2006 at the family home in suburban Clayton, Mo., starting when she was 3 and he was 12.

She said the last acts of sexual abuse and rape occurred when Sam Altman was an adult. He is now 41.

The Altman family has said Annie Altman has mental health challenges and received financial support.

Sam Altman has said she began accusing him on social media of sexual abuse after the family rejected her demands for more funds.
news.content:
پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. سام آلتمن روز سه شنبه در رد دعوی مدنی که توسط خواهرش مبنی بر متهم کردن بنیانگذار و مدیر اجرایی OpenAI به سوء استفاده جنسی مکرر بیش از دو دهه پیش ارائه شده بود، برنده شد، اتهامی که او آن را رد می کند. در رد شکایت آنی آلتمن، قاضی ناحیه ایالات متحده، زاخاری بلوستون نوشت که او علیرغم هشدارهایی مبنی بر اینکه عدم انجام این کار منجر به اخراج پرونده می شود، از حضور برای معاینه پزشکی مستقل خودداری کرده است. لورا پولیتی، وکیل آنی آلتمن، بلافاصله به درخواست برای اظهار نظر پاسخ نداد. سانتوس پرز، وکیلی که قبلاً وکالت آنی آلتمن در این پرونده را بر عهده داشت، اما در این ماه کناره گیری کرد، در بیانیه ای گفت: "من دیگر مجاز به اظهار نظر در مورد این پرونده نیستم، اما همچنان به آنی اعتقاد دارم."
وکلای سام آلتمن فوراً به درخواست اظهار نظر پاسخ ندادند. سام آلتمن پس از انتشار ربات چت ChatGPT در سال 2022 به چهره رونق هوش مصنوعی تبدیل شد. آنی آلتمن شکایت خود را در سن پترزبورگ مطرح کرد. دادگاه فدرال لوئیس در ژانویه 2025. او برادرش را متهم کرد که از سال 1997 تا 2006 در خانه خانوادگی در حومه شهر کلیتون، مونیخ، از زمانی که او 3 ساله بود و او 12 ساله بود، او را مورد آزار جنسی و تجاوز جنسی قرار داده است. او گفت که آخرین اعمال تجاوز جنسی و تجاوز جنسی زمانی رخ داد که سم آلتمن بالغ بود. او اکنون 41 سال دارد. خانواده آلتمن گفته اند که آنی آلتمن مشکلات سلامت روانی دارد و حمایت مالی دریافت کرده است. سام آلتمن گفته است که شروع به متهم کردن او در شبکه‌های اجتماعی به اتهام ابی جنسی کرده است

An unexpected shot of bad news.

A popular weight-loss shot has been recalled across the country by the FDA due to potential contamination.

The US-based compounding pharmacy that issued the initial recall back in September had already been on the agency’s radar and previously received a warning.

Apothecary Pharma, a compounding pharmacy based in North Carolina, is recalling 22 vials of their compounded tirzepatide, the active ingredient in Mounjaro and Zepbound, though these brand name drugs aren’t affected by the recall.

Even if you didn’t buy directly from Apothecary Pharma, your medication could still be affected.

The company reportedly supplies compounded tirzepatide to several telehealth providers, so check your vial’s label for the manufacturer and lot number.

Recalled vials are labeled 18 mg/mL in a 4 mL multi-dose vial.

Apothecary Pharma is also recalling a NAD+ injection, a popular longevity supplement, for possible contamination.

Both recalls are Class II, which means that using these products could cause “temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences” though severe health consequences are unlikely.

This is not the first time the FDA has disciplined Apothecary Pharma for this reason.

In December, they issued a warning letter to the company after an inspection found “serious deficiencies in your practices for producing drug products intended or expected to be sterile, which put patients at risk.”

The FDA regulates sterility at every stage of production — from cleanroom airflow and equipment cleaning to personnel gowning and filtration — not just through final-product testing.

“Lack of assurance of sterility” means the FDA cannot guarantee the product is free of contamination because of compromised sterility at some point in the production chain.

In this case, the federal agency saw operators improperly handling sterile containers, touching sterile work areas and failing to change gloves to prevent contamination, and noted visibly rusty and hard-to-clean equipment.

Compounding services like Apothecary Pharma offer alternative formulations of brand-name drugs, originally for medication shortages and specialized patient needs. However, it’s become a way for manufacturers to get around strict FDA regulations and offer steep discounts.

While most people on GLP-1s use the brand name stuff, as many as 5 million are on compounded versions. Many people get these compounded versions through telehealth companies, which ship them directly to patients.

Compounded drugs are not reviewed for safety, effectiveness or quality before they’re put on the market.

The FDA has flagged dosing errors from compounded GLP-1s that landed people in the hospital, improper storage that doesn’t keep them cool enough and even fraudulent compounded drugs listing a manufacturer that doesn’t exist.

The agency also expressed concerns about multi-dose vials, which were included in this recall, as they rely on patients to self-administer doses from a vial that could become contaminated, especially after 28 days.

The FDA has received more than 730 reports of bad reactions to compounded tirzepatide, the drug implicated in this recall — though they say this is likely underreported.
news.content: پوشش های بیشتری را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. یک عکس غیرمنتظره از اخبار بد. یک شات کاهش وزن محبوب در سراسر کشور به دلیل آلودگی احتمالی توسط FDA فراخوان شد. داروخانه ترکیبی مستقر در ایالات متحده که در ماه سپتامبر فراخوان اولیه را صادر کرد، قبلاً در رادار آژانس قرار داشت و قبلاً یک هشدار دریافت کرده بود. Apothecary Pharma، یک داروخانه ترکیبی مستقر در کارولینای شمالی، 22 ویال از tirzepatide ترکیبی خود، ماده فعال موجود در Mounjaro و Zepbound را فراخوانی می‌کند، اگرچه این داروهای نام تجاری تحت تأثیر این فراخوان قرار نمی‌گیرند. حتی اگر مستقیماً از Apothecary Pharma خریداری نکرده باشید، داروی شما همچنان ممکن است تحت تأثیر قرار گیرد. طبق گزارش‌ها، این شرکت تیرزپاتید ترکیبی را به چندین ارائه‌دهنده سلامت از راه دور عرضه می‌کند، بنابراین برچسب ویال خود را برای تولیدکننده و شماره لات بررسی کنید. ویال‌های فراخوانی شده دارای برچسب 18 میلی‌گرم در میلی‌لیتر در یک ویال چند دوز 4 میلی‌لیتری هستند. Rascón allegedly on Oct. 15 had gone to a dental office in Nogales, Sonora, where he had already received several treatment sessions.

He arrived in an agitated state and demanded to be seen without an appointment. The dentist was unable to see him, which allegedly angered the patient, who then decided to wait out in the parking lot.

Security camera video shows the brazen ambush, where Rascón stalked the doctor to his white truck and calmly shot into the open driver’s door at the dentist multiple times. Hernandez died in that parking lot.

According to investigations, the suspect blamed the dentist for leaving a tooth loose.

During the attempted warrant execution, the shootout resulted in two officers getting injured. One suffered a graze wound to the head and another had his left leg injured. Both were treated and released, officials said.

The suspect received first aid after the confrontation with Mexican authorities but died at the scene.

Rascon has had a criminal incident in his past, such as drug use and driving under the influence. Mexican authorities are coordinating with U.S. consular officials as the investigation concludes.

Rascón ظاهراً در تاریخ 15 اکتبر به دفتری که قبلاً در تاریخ 15 اکتبر سال 2018 به دفتر او رفته بود، رفته بود. چندین جلسه درمانی دریافت کرد. او با حالتی آشفته وارد شد و خواستار ملاقات بدون قرار ملاقات شد. دندانپزشک نتوانست او را ببیند، که ظاهراً باعث عصبانیت بیمار شد و او تصمیم گرفت در پارکینگ منتظر بماند. فیلم دوربین امنیتی کمین گستاخانه را نشان می دهد، جایی که راسکون دکتر را به سمت کامیون سفیدش تعقیب کرد و با آرامش چندین بار به در باز راننده دندانپزشک شلیک کرد. هرناندز در آن پارکینگ جان باخت. بر اساس تحقیقات، مظنون دندانپزشک را به دلیل لق شدن یک دندان مقصر دانسته است. در جریان اقدام به اجرای حکم، تیراندازی منجر به مجروح شدن دو مامور شد. یکی از آنها از ناحیه سر و دیگری زخمی شده بود

The annual UCL clash of the year is set as back-to-back Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain host Barcelona in a league-stage showdown Tuesday.

As expected, these two teams sit atop the UEFA standings at 2-0, with PSG’s 10 goals leading the way and Barca’s nine tied for second-best with Ashton Villa.

Both teams are masters of scoring, with PSG averaging three goals per game in their last six wins and Barca scoring 48 goals in 11 games.

PSG enters Matchday 3 in rejuvenated form and ready to defend home turf at the Parc des Princes.

The French club stumbled out of the gate and is 2-2-1 in Ligue 1, but has turned things up a notch in the league phase.

Luis Enrique’s squad opened their UCL campaign with a 6-1 win over Slovan Bratislava, then impressively beat Erling Haaland and Man City 4-2 at the Etihad Stadium last week.

Reigning Ballon d’Or winner Ousmane Dembélé, Spain’s World Cup hero Ferran Torres, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Achraf Hakimi and young star Désiré Doué lead the way.

On the other side of the field, Barça’s well-oiled machine recently beat Real Betis 5-2 to reach 11 straight wins.

Blaugrana also rallied after falling behind early to beat Galatasaray 4-1 in Turkey last Tuesday, and they made quick work of Feyenoord on UCL Matchday 1.

PSG will do everything it can to keep Hansi Flick’s squad from dominating possession because there is really no other way to keep Barca’s elaborate attack at bay.

An underlying rivalry also stems from offseason trash talk between Dembélé and Lamine Yamal over who should’ve been named Ballon d’Or last year.

Dembélé has backed his name, netting three goals and providing three assists in two UCL games. Yamal enters with one goal and four assists across two UCL fixtures.

Factor in that PSG manager Enrique played 207 games for Barca over more than eight years, rejoined as coach for another three years and led the Spain national team at the 2022 World Cup before stepping down, and this becomes appointment viewing.

Barcelona’s offseason transfer, defensive-minded Rodri, was added to the roster for moments like this, and how well he controls the midfield to give the ultra-talented front three of Yamal, Fermin Lopez and Raphinha space to operate will be key.

Riding an 11-game winning streak to start the campaign, Flick’s squad should bring their best to this early-season clash and finally get over the proverbial hump.

Bryan Kohberger’s new lawyer is taking another swing at Idaho prosecutors in his fight to have the judge who called his client a “faceless coward” removed from post-conviction proceedings.

Court-appointed attorney Greg Rauch is accusing Latah County prosecutors of “regurgitating” rules rather than addressing concerns raised in his motion to disqualify Judge Steven Hippler from the case.

Hippler said Kohberger, 31, “slithered” into the victims’ home before committing a crime that made him “the worst of the worst” after the killer admitted guilt last year.

At issue, according to Rauch, “is how [Hippler’s] statements about counsel’s preparation and [Kohberger’s] capacity for truthfulness bear on the disputes it may now decide, in combination with the myriad of other statements made.”

And when addressing the fact that there would be no allocution or explanation from Kohberger, the judge also questioned whether Kohberger even possessed the capacity to say something truthful.

“Even if I could force him to speak, which legally I cannot, how could anyone ever be assured that what he speaks is the truth?” Hippler asked during sentencing. “Do we really believe, after all of this, he is capable of speaking the truth, or of giving up something of himself to help the very people whose lives he destroyed? Rather, I suspect the so-called reason would be dished out in enticing self-serving and aggrandizing untruthful bits, leaving people wanting more information, more insight, and thus enhancing even further the power he seeks to hold.”

Rauch wrote that “of course” judges can deny defense motions, “condemn terrible crimes,” and go on to preside over post-conviction claims.

“The question is not whether someone might criticize the Court, but whether an informed, reasonable observer could question its impartiality in light of this connected record,” he wrote.

And it’s not just that Hippler tore into Kohberger at sentencing. He has also taken issue with a June scheduling order days before Kohberger surprised the country and pleaded guilty to avoid the death penalty.

“This motion does not rest upon one adverse ruling, one harsh statement, or the mere fact that the judge who presided over Bryan Kohberger’s criminal case has been assigned to his post-conviction proceeding,” Rauch wrote in his initial 22-page motion on Aug. 27. “It rests upon the extraordinary convergence of all of them.”

Hippler had rejected a request for more time for Kohberger’s previous defense lawyer, Anne Taylor, and in a June 26 order, described her complaints about discovery as “ultimately empty” while suggesting she was simply trying to delay his trial.

Six days later, at a change-of-plea hearing, Hippler asked Taylor, “Have you been able to do all the discovery you feel necessary?”

“Yes, Your Honor,” she replied.

Prosecutors, in an opposition to the motion filed earlier this month, wrote that Kohberger had failed to show Hippler “is biased.”

Outgoing Latah County Prosecuting Attorney Bill Thompson, who announced his retirement earlier this week, and Deputy Prosecuting Attorney Keith Scholl wrote that Hippler’s statements about Kohberger after he’d admitted to killing four innocent students were not unusual or out of line.

“In our case, the sentencing remarks are not enough to show bias, and the required showing of perceived bias cannot be tied to this Court’s capacity to fairly adjudicate any [post-conviction relief] claims alleged in this case but rather puts this Court in the best position to adjudicate them as the legislature and the Idaho Supreme Court’s rules intend,” they wrote.

Rauch also argued that Hippler could voluntarily recuse himself from the case to avoid any appearance of partiality.

In the new 12-page filing, Rauch also argued that prosecutors have attributed concessions to his client that were never made, mischaracterized his initial motion and failed to address some of the arguments he did make in it.

“The State’s Response does not resolve this motion by repeating the ordinary rule, supplying concessions Petitioner never made, or calling the disputed statements routine,” Rauch wrote.

Kohberger is attempting to undo his guilty plea in the University of Idaho student murders that killed Madison Mogen, 21, Kaylee Goncalves, 21, Xana Kernodle, 20, and Ethan Chapin, 20, in November 2022.

The former criminology Ph.D. student initially filed a handwritten petition for post-conviction relief in July.

“The State’s Response does not resolve this motion by repeating the ordinary rule, supplying concessions Petitioner never made, or calling the disputed statements routine,” Rauch wrote.

“A request for an impartial adjudicator is certainly not a request for a sympathetic one,” he wrote. “Reassignment would change the judge, not the evidence or the governing law.”

A hearing on the matter was supposed to take place Thursday, before Hippler abruptly canceled it and said it would be rescheduled later.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Joel Angel Juarez/Getty Images)

Two Democratic areas in Texas posted record-breaking first-day early voting numbers Monday, which could spell trouble for Republicans.

Dallas and Harris County had more voters than ever when early voting began Monday, which was a good sign for Democratic Texas Senate nominee James Talarico. Judge Clay Jenkins, who has access to official data from the Dallas County Elections Department, reported that 76,069 voters showed up in Dallas County, which surpassed the previous record of 60,573 voters in 2020.

The number of registered voters in Dallas surged from 1,398,469 in 2020 to 1,463,708 this year, a 4.7% rise.

Former Vice President Kamala Harris won Dallas County by a 60.1% to 38.1% margin in the 2024 presidential election, according to Politico. Former Democratic Texas Senate nominee Colin Allred won the county by 29 points against Republican Texas Sen. Ted Cruz. (RELATED: Republicans Pour $30,000,000 Into Ken Paxton’s Campaign During Final Stretch Of Red-State Race)

@DallasElections For context the first day vote is up significantly in Dallas County when you compare it to the last Trump midterm in 2018. 2018- 59,388 2026-76,079

The number of voters in Dallas County already surpassed turnout during the 2024 presidential election, according to The Political HQ.

The Harris County Elections Department recorded over 100,000 in-person voters. As of 3:30 pm central time, over 70,000 voters had been processed, which surpassed the previous record of 63,188 votes recorded in the 2018 midterm elections. Harris County includes the city of Houston.

“Harris County has broken the record for first-day early voting turnout in a midterm election!As of 3:30 p.m., 70K+ voters have been processed, surpassing the previous record of 63,188 set in 2018, with 3.5 hours remaining,” the Harris County Elections Department said on X.

Day 1 of Early Voting: As of October 19, 2026, #HarrisCounty has recorded 104.6K + total In-Person Early Voters for the November 3 General & Special Elections. 🗳️✅ #harrisvotes https://t.co/vXRFWBtTSs

The county’s number of registered voters rose 14.7%, from 2,357,199 in 2018 to 2,702,952 this year, according to county data.

Harris won Harris County by a five-point margin, 51.9% to 46.5%, according to Politico.

Over 22,000 voters turned out in El Paso County, the second-highest turnout number on record for the first day of early voting. The historically blue county had its highest ever first-day voter turnout in the 2018 midterm election when 24,449 were recorded. Harris won in El Paso County by 15 points, according to Politico.

Collin County, Denton County and Tarrant County reported increased voter turnout in comparison to the previous election in 2022, which are all historically Republican counties. Collins County reported over 34,000 voters on the first day of early voting, which was well above the roughly 19,000 voters on the first day of early voting in 2022, according to Fox 4 KDFW, a local Fox affiliate.

The county reported approximately 43,000 voters on the first day of early voting in 2024, according to Fox 4 KDFW.

Denton County reported over 34,000 voters on the first day, which surpassed turnout in 2018 and 2022.

Republican PACs spent over $326 million to support Republican Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton while he fell behind Talarico in the polls. Talarico led by an average of 2.2 points as of Tuesday, according to RealClearPolling.

Paxton told donors in leaked audio that the Iran war and gas prices caused his campaign to struggle.

The PACs spent unprecedented amounts in other red states, including Kansas, South Dakota, South Carolina and Iowa.

دو منطقه دموکرات در تگزاس روز دوشنبه رکورد شکستن تعداد رای‌گیری زودهنگام را ثبت کردند که می‌تواند برای جمهوری‌خواهان دردسر ایجاد کند. زمانی که رای‌گیری زودهنگام روز دوشنبه آغاز شد، دالاس و هریس کانتی رای دهندگان بیشتری نسبت به همیشه داشتند که این نشانه خوبی برای جیمز تالاریکو، نامزد دموکرات سنای تگزاس بود. قاضی کلی جنکینز که به اطلاعات رسمی اداره انتخابات شهرستان دالاس دسترسی دارد، گزارش داد که 76069 رای دهنده در شهرستان دالاس شرکت کردند که از رکورد قبلی 60573 رای دهنده در سال 2020 فراتر رفت. 4.7 درصد افزایش. معاون رئیس جمهور سابق کامالا هریس با 60.1 درصد به 38 برنده شهرستان دالاس شد. به گزارش پولیتیکو، 1 درصد اختلاف در انتخابات ریاست جمهوری 2024. کالین آلرد، نامزد سابق دموکرات سنای تگزاس، با 29 امتیاز در مقابل تد کروز، سناتور جمهوریخواه تگزاس پیروز این شهرستان شد. (مرتبط: جمهوری خواهان 30،000،000 دلار به کمپین کن پکستون در طول آخرین مرحله مسابقه ایالت سرخ می ریزند)
@DallasElections برای زمینه، رای روز اول در شهرستان دالاس به میزان قابل توجهی افزایش یافته است، وقتی آن را با آخرین میان دوره ای ترامپ در سال 2018 مقایسه کنید. 2018- 59,388 2026-76,079
بر اساس گزارش ستاد سیاسی، تعداد رای دهندگان در شهرستان دالاس در طول انتخابات ریاست جمهوری 2024 از شرکت کنندگان فراتر رفته است. اداره انتخابات شهرستان هریس بیش از 100000 رای دهنده حضوری را ثبت کرده است. تا ساعت 3:30 بعد از ظهر به وقت مرکزی، بیش از 70000 رای دهنده مورد رسیدگی قرار گرفته اند که از زمان قبلی فراتر رفته است.

news.originalContent:
Calls for independence intensified last year, with some 300,000 petitioning officials for a referendum.

Voters in Alberta have chosen to remain part of Canada in a first-ever independence referendum.

Canadian state broadcaster CBC News called the results of Monday’s vote late on the same day after 48 percent of the ballots counted showed overwhelming support for the “remain” side, with 76 percent opting to stay with Canada.

The result marks a major win for Prime Minister Mark Carney, who is facing a trade and political war with the United States amid US President Donald Trump’s higher tariffs and repeated suggestions of annexing the country.

On his way into a cabinet meeting on Tuesday morning, Carney called it a “great day.”

“I’m thrilled that Albertans have chosen unity. They’ve chosen to build together. They’ve chosen to continue to take care of each other, to move forward together with purpose,” he said.

But the result also comes as a disappointment for those Albertans seeking independence for the resource-rich region following years of grievances laid at Ottawa’s door. Here’s what we know:

The nonbinding referendum was first announced in May following a campaign and petition by a group of Albertans who want to be an independent country.

While only about one-third of Albertans were found to be pro-independence in polls, Alberta Premier Danielle Smith argued in her announcement that a referendum was necessary to respect the 300,000 Albertans who had petitioned officials for it.

In the referendum, voters answered 10 questions, including whether the government should begin a binding process to seek independence from Canada. They also answered questions on immigration, access to provincial services like education, social care and healthcare, and voter identification requirements.

Prime Minister Carney had campaigned for Albertans to vote “remain”, saying last week at a rally in Calgary that separation would be “ a dangerous bluff that will lead to years of deep division”.

“There are some outside our borders who are working to break us so they can own us,” he said.

Researchers have pointed to possible online influence campaigns by both Russian and US entities that helped amplify the call for separation and allegedly shared misleading information. Alberta PM Smith told media in August that the online activity was under observation.

Prime Minister Carney, who grew up in the region, said “Albertans made a clear choice” in a statement he made early on Tuesday.

“They chose unity, to build together, and to take care of each other,” he said, adding that “Canadians will move forward together with renewed purpose and high ambition.”

Alberta’s Premier Smith said she was pleased to see the results and that “Albertans have voted for a stronger Alberta in a united Canada.”

Separatist leaders from the groups Let Alberta Decide, the Alberta Prosperity Project and the Pathway to Independence said they will wait for all votes to be counted before conceding.

First Nations groups turned out in strong numbers to vote to remain with Canada, with one southern Alberta polling station in an area home to the Siksika Nation temporarily running out of ballots, local media reported.

Many Albertans have long complained that their critical natural resources are funding the government in Ottawa and the commercial hubs of Toronto and Montreal, but that the province does not receive proportionate benefits.

The province, with a population of 5.1 million, holds massive oil deposits. It also holds reserves of critical and rare-earth metals including lithium, titanium and zircon, which are essential for manufacturing many tech items, from smartphones to fighter jets.

Separatist movements, some of which even support Alberta joining the US, go back to the 1940s, following the discovery of oil reserves. Some of Alberta’s premiers have had spats with Ottawa over wealth distribution.

US President Trump has made remarks about Canada becoming a US state in recent months.

Last week, he told a political rally in the US state of Arizona that Canada will “end up being the 51st state, because it’s the only way it works”.

The two countries have been embroiled in a trade war since talks fell apart in August this year and they slapped each other with tit-for-tat tariffs.

Earlier this month, tech billionaire Elon Musk called for Alberta, Saskatchewan and Quebec to separate from Canada, saying “they’d be better off”.

But the matter of Alberta’s independence gained intense scrutiny last year after pro-separatists launched a petition to pressure the government.

Alberta, alongside other western provinces of British Columbia, Saskatchewan and Manitoba, have all complained about “western alienation” by the government in the centre.

With separatism agitations running so far back, experts say the referendum will likely not end the movement altogether.

Ahead of the vote, some separatist leaders said they would pursue another referendum if necessary, arguing that the referendum shows that independence is legally possible.

“Regardless of what happens on Monday, we’ve already won,” Keith Wilson, co-leader of Let Alberta Decide, said at a rally last week.
news.content:
درخواست‌ها برای استقلال در سال گذشته تشدید شد و حدود 300000 نفر از مقامات برای برگزاری همه‌پرسی درخواست کردند. رأی‌دهندگان در آلبرتا تصمیم گرفتند در اولین همه‌پرسی استقلال، بخشی از کانادا باقی بمانند. شبکه تلویزیونی دولتی کانادا در اواخر همان روز نتایج رای‌گیری روز دوشنبه را پس از آن که 48 درصد آرا شمارش شد، نشان داد که «حزب موافق با 7 درصد حمایت قاطع از 7 درصد» باقی ماندند. کانادا این نتیجه یک پیروزی بزرگ برای نخست وزیر مارک کارنی است، که در بحبوحه تعرفه های بالاتر دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا و پیشنهادات مکرر برای الحاق این کشور با یک جنگ تجاری و سیاسی با ایالات متحده مواجه است. کارنی در راه ورود به جلسه کابینه در صبح سه شنبه، آن را "روز عالی" خواند.
"من هیجان زده هستم که آلبرتایی ها اتحاد را انتخاب کرده اند. آنها تصمیم گرفته اند با هم بسازند. آنها تصمیم گرفته‌اند که به مراقبت از یکدیگر ادامه دهند، تا با هدف پیشروی کنند.» اما این نتیجه برای آن دسته از آلبرتایی‌هایی که به دنبال استقلال برای منطقه غنی از منابع پس از سال‌ها نارضایتی در اتاوا هستند، ناامیدکننده است.
همه پرسی غیر الزام آور اولین بار در ماه مه پس از کمپین و درخواست گروهی از آلبرتایی ها که می خواهند کشوری مستقل باشند، اعلام شد. در حالی که در نظرسنجی‌ها تنها حدود یک سوم آلبرتای‌ها طرفدار استقلال بودند، دانیل اسمیت، نخست‌وزیر آلبرتا در اعلامیه‌اش استدلال کرد که برای احترام به 300000 آلبرتایی که درخواست کرده بودند، همه‌پرسی لازم است.

news.originalContent:
With new talk of escalation, Islamabad is trying to revive negotiations without alienating Tehran, Riyadh or Washington.

Islamabad, Pakistan – Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, arrived in Tehran on Tuesday evening for talks with Iranian officials, as diplomatic efforts ramp up to prevent a new round of fighting with the United States and Israel.

Munir’s visit is his fifth to Iran since the April ceasefire between Tehran and Washington, which was brokered by Islamabad. Pakistan’s Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi is accompanying Munir, Iran’s state news agency IRNA reported. The Pakistani army chief is expected to meet Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi first, IRNA said.

The visit comes a day after Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov held talks in Tehran, and two weeks after Pakistan and its allies agreed to accelerate the deployment of forces to Saudi Arabia, which has come under repeated attacks from the Iran-backed Houthi armed group in Yemen.

Lavrov’s visit on Monday was his first to Tehran since the start of the US-Israel war on Iran in February. The Russian foreign minister met Araghchi and President Masoud Pezeshkian, and the talks covered the war, the Strait of Hormuz and efforts to end the fighting.

“The timing of [Munir’s] visit, following Lavrov’s presence in Tehran, suggests that Iran prefers to keep multiple diplomatic channels open, rather than relying exclusively on a single mediator,” Seyed Mojtaba Jalazadeh, a Tehran-based foreign policy analyst, told Al Jazeera.

But the Munir visit also comes at a time when some experts have warned of growing signs that United States President Donald Trump might be preparing for a return to fighting with Iran. Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to end the war on September 26. Since then, the US has deployed an additional aircraft carrier to the Middle East, which is expected to arrive by late November. Trump has endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Israel’s upcoming October 27 election, referring to their shared mission in attacking Iran. Trump said that if Netanyahu were not re-elected, the US would need to attack Iran on its own.

Analysts say these developments add urgency to diplomatic efforts to sidestep a potential military escalation. In recent weeks, Qatar has played a key role in channeling proposals between the US and Iran. Andreas Krieg, an associate professor in security studies at King’s College London, told Al Jazeera that while Qatar increasingly provides the diplomatic machinery behind the talks, Doha still values Islamabad’s access to Washington and Tehran.

“Pakistan offers political access, particularly through Field Marshal Asim Munir, while Qatar does much of the detailed negotiating,” Krieg said.

Pakistan has mediated between Washington and Tehran since the US and Israel began striking Iran on February 28.

Islamabad brokered a ceasefire on April 8 and, days later, hosted the highest-level direct engagement between the US and Iran since 1979.

In June, the two sides agreed to a 14-point memorandum of understanding (MoU).

Under the agreement, the US was to lift its naval blockade within 30 days, the Strait of Hormuz was to reopen, and about $24bn in estimated frozen Iranian assets was to be released in phases over 60 days of further talks, including negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme.

That period expired in mid-August without either side agreeing to extend it. Iran says the US failed to meet its commitments, and Tehran has kept the Strait of Hormuz closed, insisting that Washington first lift the blockade.

Pakistan’s Foreign Office has continued to point to the agreement and its utility.

“The Islamabad MoU is already in place, and some of the points currently under discussion are fully aligned with it,” spokesman Sajjad Haider Khan told a weekly briefing on October 9.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on October 2 that Iran’s seven-day plan was drawn from the MoU.

Analysts, however, disagree on whether the agreement can still provide a basis for negotiations.

“On the Islamabad MoU, I think it’s done from both sides and perhaps a new mechanism is required to start negotiations,” Umer Karim, an associate fellow at the King Faisal Centre for Research and Islamic Studies in Riyadh, told Al Jazeera.

Krieg said that while the Islamabad MoU was “politically alive”, it was “operationally dead”.

“The circumstances under which it was signed have fundamentally changed,” he said.

But Muhammad Faisal, a South Asia security researcher at the University of Technology Sydney, said the agreement could still be used.

“The Islamabad MoU remains usable, even if the political and security environment has deteriorated,” he told Al Jazeera. “It is still the minimum agreed benchmark between Washington and Tehran, and neither side has an obvious alternative framework for addressing the issues related to maritime access, sanctions relief and nuclear talks.”

Meanwhile, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on August 7.

It was Pakistan’s second defence pact with Saudi Arabia, after the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement the two countries signed in September 2025.

At an emergency meeting in Riyadh on October 5, the three countries agreed to expedite the deployment of forces and capabilities under the pact.

Within days, Houthi missiles and drones struck Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport more than once, as well as targets in Abha, Yanbu and Shaybah.

Lieutenant-General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, the Pakistani military’s spokesman, discussed the defence pact and the importance of protecting holy sites in Mecca and Medina in an interview with Independent Arabia on October 18.

“The security of the Harmain Sharifain is paramount. It’s non-negotiable,” he said, referring to Islam’s two holiest mosques. “Whatever support is needed to do that is being provided and will be provided.”

He declined to provide details, citing operational confidentiality.

Chaudhry said Pakistan wanted a negotiated end to the conflict. “If we are unable to come to a negotiated outcome and we turn into a military conflict, then this collective deterrence, this instrument of collective deterrence of Mecca Alliance will definitely come into play, as it is coming into play,” he said.

Asked at the October 9 briefing whether Pakistani forces in Saudi Arabia would engage the Houthis, Foreign Office spokesman Khan said they would not.

“These forces would not cross the border into Yemen to launch attacks against the Houthis,” he said.

On Monday, a day before leaving for Tehran, Munir met Saudi ambassador to Pakistan, Rajeh Tami Albugamy. A statement said the two expressed satisfaction with progress under the pact, but made no mention of the Houthis or Iran.

Tehran’s public response to the agreement has largely been restrained. On October 11, Araghchi told his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan, that Tehran was ready to provide “any possible assistance” to start a dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen, IRNA reported.

Saudi state media said that the two only discussed the “recent escalation in violence in the region”.

After meeting Iranian leaders in New York last month, Dar said they had told him Iran had nothing to do with the Houthis and had suggested engaging them politically rather than militarily.

But Krieg said Pakistan’s two roles were becoming harder to reconcile.

“Pakistan remains an important intermediary, but its credibility as a neutral actor is increasingly compromised by its security commitments to Saudi Arabia,” he said.

Jalazadeh said Tehran’s concern was more limited.

“Iran does not necessarily perceive stronger defence cooperation between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia as an immediate threat, but it does regard it as a complicating and constraining factor,” he said.

But it’s not just Pakistan facing competing pressures — or sending seemingly mixed signals.

In Washington, Trump has pledged not to strike Iran before the US midterm elections.

“We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the US on November 3rd,” he wrote on his Truth Social platform on October 8. In the same post, he said the US was having productive discussions with Iran. The naval blockade has remained in place.

Ten days later, though, Trump endorsed Netanyahu. “If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so,” Trump wrote.

On Monday, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met Netanyahu at Ovda airbase in southern Israel during an unannounced visit, Axios reported. The outlet said the visit came amid US-Israeli discussions about potentially resuming major combat operations against Iran.

“Threats of military strikes, combined with the blockade and indirect negotiations, undermine Iran’s confidence in Washington’s intentions and make stronger security guarantees one of the central issues in any potential agreement,” Jalazadeh said.

Faisal told Al Jazeera that the timing of the two votes, a week apart, made major concessions difficult for both sides and raised the risk of escalation.

Krieg said the elections were among the strongest constraints on another major war, but warned that the risk could grow once they had passed.

“The immediate danger is that Iran overplays its hand,” he said. “A major attack causing American casualties could override electoral calculations altogether.”

Below is State of the Day, a morning newsletter from the Daily Caller Editorial Desk. Sign up here.__________

Welcome to State of the Day,

Prepare yourselves; it’ll be a bloodbath for control,

The Conservative Establishment Is Planning For A Post-Trump GOP

More than 500 conservative officials, election administrators, policymakers, and civic leaders.

More than 30 gatherings across 20-plus states. And, for the most part, conversations happening behind closed doors.

That’s the picture Johns Hopkins University’s SNF Agora Institute and the R Street Institute painted in a report published this September, detailing three years of work to build what they call the “Civic Right” — a network of Republicans claiming to be focused on election trust, governing institutions, and the future of their movement.

The initiative’s organizers argue that conservatives need better infrastructure to connect leaders and turn their ideas into sustained political action.

Not exactly the most eye-catching stuff, but it offers a glimpse into the fight over what comes next for the Republican Party, a fight that is playing out beyond the boundaries of Washington’s catfights.

For some, the party’s future means doubling down on Donald Trump’s MAGA movement. For others, it means returning to the old guard of neoconservatism. And for others still, it means turning the page on both and looking for a new cause that’ll resonate with everyday Americans.

Amid all this, the mysterious Civic Right has been meeting privately to discuss what comes next.

The meetings aren’t exactly riveting. There are no stadium rallies, no viral clips, and no grand declaration of war against the current state of the Republican Party.

Instead, there’s an assortment of state officials, local political networks, policy groups, and grant money — the unsightly machinery that shapes politics before any of us even realize it.

The project is led by Scott Warren at Johns Hopkins’ SNF Agora Institute, with R Street’s Matt Germer among its authors. R Street president and co-founder Eli Lehrer came up through the Heritage Foundation, the American Enterprise Institute, and the Heartland Institute, and once wrote speeches for then-Senate Majority Leader Bill Frist.

In other words, this isn’t some grassroots revolt bubbling up from the ranks. It’s an organized effort by longtime center-right policy hands to build a network around their vision.

And there’s money behind the machinery, too. In June 2026, Carnegie Corporation of New York awarded Johns Hopkins $500,000 to support its Conservative Agenda for Democracy program.

Separately, public grant records show that R Street received millions in grants between 2018 and 2025, including $7.1 million from the William and Flora Hewlett Foundation, $2.4 million from the Pew Charitable Trusts, and $935,000 from the Charles Koch Institute.

Charles Koch’s funding network has supported open borders and foreign labor, drawing criticism from both sides of the aisle. In a 2015 interview with Vox, Sen. Bernie Sanders quipped, “Open borders? No, that’s a Koch brothers proposal.”

Sanders went on to correctly argue that businesses benefit from an expanded pool of workers willing to accept rock-bottom wages, which puts pressure on American workers and drives down pay; see cheap foreign labor.

And the Koch brothers aren’t alone. The William and Flora Hewlett Foundation, R Street’s largest reported funder, published a defense of expanded migration, arguing that greater opportunities to move abroad are among the fastest ways to raise living standards.

That’s just a taste of the sort of backers this venture boasts; take all the time you need to really breathe in that ripe swamp stench.

MAGA, on the other hand, offers a different vision, one built around Trump himself. His endorsements, feuds, and demands for loyalty have become defining features of the movement. The populist uprising that promised to take on the establishment has developed its own hierarchy, with Trump at the top.

But with Trump set to leave the presidency after 2028, the movement built around him faces its own identity crisis.

And don’t forget about the disaffected Republicans, as I like to call them, essentially the Thomas Massies and Marjorie Taylor Greenes of the world.

They’re conservatives who don’t neatly fit into either category, but are instead charting a path of their own. A mix of libertarian, conservative, and pragmatic policies makes up the third camp in the war for control.

Who’s to say who’ll come out on top?

The fight won’t just be about who’s the GOP nominee in ‘28; it’s about who has the money, networks, and local infrastructure to turn their vision of the Republican Party into reality.

While everyone argues over the future of the right, some are quietly building it.

How Jared And Ivanka Sparked A Revolution, Daily Caller, John Loftus

The Daily Caller’s John Loftus offers new reporting on the mounting backlash against Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump — along with their political allies in the Albanian government — over a private real estate deal to develop Sazan Island. Riots have broken out in the Albanian capital of Tiranë over what citizens see as a corrupt land deal that has given Kushner and Trump—along with partnered investors—control over the island.

Anthropic Floats Bill That Would Let Feds Step In Only When More Than 50 Lives Are On The Line, Daily Caller News Foundation, Dylan Kresak

Artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic is lobbying Congress to back legislation that would ostensibly limit the Commerce Department’s regulatory oversight of the technology. The Artificial Intelligence Evaluation, Governance, and Incident Safety (AEGIS) Act would only allow federal regulators to step in and shut down an AI model once it has threatened to kill more than 50 people or cause over $1 billion in damage.

Putin Floats a Summit With Trump and Xi to Discuss Ukraine Deal, The Wall Street Journal, Lingling Wei, Alex Leary, Thomas Grove and Josh Dawsey

The Wall Street Journal reported that Vladimir Putin has floated a summit with President Trump and China’s Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. The proposal comes as Washington and Beijing are embroiled in a race to lead the AI frontier. The plan could give Beijing a larger role in negotiations on European security, as Putin seeks to capitalize on warming ties with Trump.

Cattle Ranchers Are Getting Grilled 30 Days Into Trump’s Foreign Beef Blitz, Daily Caller, John Loftus

President Donald Trump’s decision to waive tariffs on beef imports from Argentina is costing American ranchers dearly. Just 30 days after the waiver was implemented, “prices paid for live and dressed cutter cows, which compete directly against the lean beef imports, have fallen 12.2 percent and 13.9 percent, respectively,” the watchdog group Farm Action reports. This price drop is significantly affecting American ranchers, who are already hard-pressed by rising diesel prices.

news.originalContent:
The UK’s new prime minister has made big promises and is a popular leader, but there is still talk of an early election.

Andy Burnham’s UK foreign policy tested by Brexit, US ties and Iran war

London, United Kingdom – There was a moment towards the end of Andy Burnham’s conference speech in Liverpool that, through silence, spoke volumes.

The new prime minister and Labour leader fell quiet.

For 20 seconds he stood, saying nothing. He hadn’t forgotten his words. He was gathering his emotions for a passage of the speech he hadn’t been able to make it through in rehearsals without crying.

Burnham’s father had died just a couple of weeks before, and this was the section where he’d talk about it.

As the audience realised what was coming they stood, applauding, and urging him on with shouts of “Come on, lad!’ and “Come on, Andy!”

Thanking them, he composed himself and continued.

Conference speeches are theatre, and contemporary British political standards require that a leader be relatable. But there’s little doubt that Andy Burnham handled this moment with an emotional register that struck many as genuine.

His predecessor Keir Starmer sometimes came across as wooden, almost robotic and uncomfortable in front of cameras. Burnham, the seventh prime minister in 10 years, is more emotional.

He talks big ideas and grand solutions and relishes the opportunity to communicate.

In the vibes-denominated currency of modern political discourse, this matters.

The polls speak for themselves. Politico’s Poll of Polls had the Labour Party retake top spot shortly after Burnham became PM – a position it has not relinquished since. At the end of September, Ipsos found Andy Burnham to be the only politician with a positive net favourability rating.

YouGov’s polling also judges him the most popular politician in the UK at the moment.

But to keep up, Burnham must deliver tangible change before the next general election. Unless he calls one early, that will be 2029.

According to political analyst Sam Freedman, “So many in Westminster keep coming back to an early election, despite Burnham ruling it out … No one can quite figure out how Burnham keeps the hope vibe going for three more years with relatively little visible progress.”

In the Welsh town of Port Talbot, terraces of workers’ cottages cluster beside the UK’s largest steelworks.

Like much of Wales, Port Talbot did vote Labour for a century – until elections for the Senedd Cymru or Welsh Parliament in May.

Labour was beaten to an unprecedented third place behind Plaid Cymru’s nationalists, and the anti-immigration Reform UK.

But that was before Burnham took over.

Myles Lewis, who organises social walks for the town’s elderly, told Al Jazeera that Labour had not convinced people on immigration, and Starmer’s communication wasn’t good enough.

“[But now], it’s kind of going back to what Labour was in the 50s and 60s, where they actually looked after the working-class people. I do believe Andy Burnham can get there because I think he has the interests of the working-class people.”

In his first weeks in power, Burnham delivered a quick flurry of eye-catching, domestic, cost-of-living-focused policies.

He capped bus fares, cut the value-added tax (VAT) on electricity bills, and cut business rates for pubs.

He said that he would end street homelessness, reindustrialise the country, take services back into public control, and start the biggest build-out of social housing since World War II.

The mayor of Greater Manchester for nine years, Burnham supports the devolution of powers from Westminster to the UK’s nations and regions.

In July, he announced mayors could keep a share of business rates from April 2027 and of income tax from 2028.

And his conference speech in September set out the contours of some big political battles to come, including a national social care service, free at the point of use, paid for by changing the UK pensions’ triple lock from 2030. It would arrive next parliament. Burnham also pitched a national commission on electoral reform, with a manifesto commitment to overhaul the voting system. And he delivered a blunt verdict on Brexit: that it “has done more harm than good”. He wouldn’t rule out an in-out referendum, or a pledge for the UK to rejoin the European Union, in Labour’s next manifesto, he said.

On foreign affairs, there is less blue water between Burnham and his predecessors.

When he travelled to Ukraine in August, the UK’s new prime minister came with a headline-grabbing gift – British know-how to build the long-range SCALP missile. He was the fourth British prime minister to visit Kyiv since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and pledge steadfast support.

On Gaza, he has said the Labour government “didn’t get it right” and should have called for a ceasefire earlier. And in September, the Burnham government announced a sanctions package against illegal West Bank settlements.

But there has been no genocide declaration, and no full arms embargo against Israel. And Burnham hasn’t overturned the Starmer government’s proscription of the Palestine Action protest group as a “terrorist” organisation.

Defence spending is also a looming problem.

The government’s formal defence pledge is 3.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2035, and Burnham has declined to say whether he’d pay for it with tax rises or welfare cuts.

John Healey, who resigned as the UK’s defence secretary in June over underfunding, is now chancellor of the exchequer, and will not commit to the 3-percent-by-2030 target he set himself.

Burnham’s first budget comes at the end of this month. A full spending review follows next year. Much will be clearer after these.

His biggest pledges – reindustrialisation, control of public services, a new social care system – are expensive.

Burnham certainly has the vibes. The public likes them, for now. The budget will show whether he can afford them.

نخست‌وزیر جدید بریتانیا وعده‌های بزرگی داده و رهبر محبوبی است، اما هنوز صحبت از برگزاری انتخابات زودهنگام است.
لندن، بریتانیا - لحظه ای نزدیک به پایان سخنرانی کنفرانس اندی برنهام در لیورپول بود که در سکوت، حرف های زیادی زد. نخست وزیر جدید و رهبر حزب کارگر ساکت شدند. او به مدت 20 ثانیه ایستاد و چیزی نگفت. حرف هایش را فراموش نکرده بود. او داشت احساساتش را برای قسمتی از سخنرانی جمع می کرد که نتوانسته بود در تمرینات بدون گریه انجامش دهد. پدر برنهام فقط چند هفته قبل فوت کرده بود، و این قسمتی بود که او در مورد آن صحبت می کرد. وقتی حضار متوجه شدند که چه چیزی در راه است، ایستادند، کف زدند و با فریادهای "بیا و بیا!"
با تشکر از آنها، خود را جمع و جور کرد و ادامه داد. سخنرانی های کنفرانس تئاتر است و استانداردهای سیاسی معاصر بریتانیا مستلزم این است که یک رهبر قابل ارتباط باشد. اما شکی وجود ندارد که اندی برنهام این لحظه را با یک ثبت احساسی که بسیاری را به‌عنوان واقعی برانگیخت، اداره کرد. سلف او، کیر استارمر، گاهی اوقات به‌عنوان چوبی، تقریباً روباتیک و ناراحت‌کننده جلوی دوربین‌ها مواجه می‌شد. برنهام، هفتمین نخست وزیر در 10 سال اخیر، احساساتی تر است. او از ایده‌های بزرگ و راه‌حل‌های بزرگ صحبت می‌کند و از فرصتی برای برقراری ارتباط لذت می‌برد. در گفتمان سیاسی مدرن، این موضوع اهمیت دارد.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by NATHAN HOWARD/POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Vice President J.D. Vance said Monday he would not endorse Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in an interview with journalist Mark Halperin.

President Donald Trump offered Netanyahu his full endorsement Sunday ahead of Israel’s elections later this month.

“I endorse American candidates, and that’s where I’m focused on is the midterm,” Vance told Halperin aboard Air Force Two. “I’m not getting involved in Israeli elections.”

“I’m not anti-endorsing him. I’m not pro-endorsing him. I’m not getting involved in Israeli elections,” the vice president added.

Netanyahu is facing several challengers this election year, including Gadi Eisenkot, Yair Lapid, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, Yair Golan and Avigdor Liberman, all of whom are members of the opposition bloc. Recent polls show that Eisenkot and the Yashar party have a slight lead over Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party, but neither faction appears to have enough support yet to secure a 61-seat majority in the Knesset.

Trump on Sunday described the Israeli prime minister as a “Great Warrior and an even greater Partner for Peace in combatting [sic] the Islamic Republic of Iran.”

“If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself … This is the kind of Partner that the United States of America is demanding of Israel, a Country for which it has done so much.”

During a recent interview with Fox News host Mark Levin, Netanyahu said that, if he wins re-election, his first goal would be to “achieve the complete elimination of the Iranian threat to Israel, to America, and to the world.” (RELATED: 45 Seconds Into Softball Interview, Netanyahu Tells Mark Levin He Wants To Drag The US Even Deeper Into Iran War)

“This is a regime that chants ‘death to Israel,’ ‘death to America’ — you’re the real target,” Netanyahu told Levin. “I think we are well on our way to achieving this with President Trump’s brilliant leadership, both militarily and then economic blockade, very effective. Let’s complete the job and have the people of Iran seize their own future. It changes the Middle East.”

Vance previously campaigned with Hungary’s then-prime minister, Viktor Orban, in Budapest days before the national election in April, which Orban lost. The vice president said he wanted “to help [Orban] in this campaign cycle” but that the U.S. would “work with whoever wins this election.”

news.originalContent:
UNICEF says escalating fighting in Taiz is threatening its water systems, serving an estimated three million people.

More than 250,000 people have been internally displaced in Yemen since the country’s war reignited in July, the United Nations Refugee Agency (UNHCR) has said, as fighting between Houthi rebels and forces loyal to the internationally recognised government rages across several fronts.

The city of Taiz in southwestern Yemen is at the centre of the displacement crisis, accounting for 76 percent of departures and hosting 52 percent of those newly displaced, UNHCR said in a statement on Tuesday.

Lahij in southwestern Yemen hosts 23 percent of the newly displaced population, followed by Aden in the south with 13 percent, UNHCR said.

“Shelling intensified in Taiz, including in residential areas and around health facilities, while insecurity and restrictions along key routes continue to constrain humanitarian access and movement,” the agency said in a statement.

The Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), have encircled Taiz since early October, blocking the road that links it to Aden, the interim capital of the Saudi-backed internationally recognised government.

“The most immediate needs that we’ve been able to identify are around shelter, food, and multi-purpose cash assistance,” UNHCR spokesperson Matthew Saltmarsh told a news conference in Geneva, Switzerland.

The agency said about 33,700 families still require shelter assistance amid severe underfunding of the humanitarian response to the war.

Separately, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said in a statement that escalating fighting and fuel shortages in Taiz are threatening its water systems that serve an estimated three million people, including at least 1.6 million children.

“Already one of Yemen’s most water-scarce areas, Taiz is now facing renewed pressure on its most essential services for thousands of displaced families,” said Akhil Iyer, UNICEF’s Yemen representative, at a press briefing in Geneva.

The warnings come as fighting intensifies between Saudi-backed government forces and the Iran-aligned Houthis.

The death toll from a Houthi ballistic missile strike on a military training camp in Yemen’s Shabwa governorate increased to at least 58, local authorities said.

The Yemeni government described the site as a security training centre away from the front lines, while Houthi forces said they targeted Saudi-backed forces. Hospitals faced blood shortages in Ataq as medical teams responded to casualties and families searched for missing relatives.

The attack was followed by retaliatory strikes by government forces near Taiz, raising further concerns over the worsening humanitarian crisis in Yemen.

Reporting from the capital, Sanaa, Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry said, “The Houthis are not backing down. Their military spokesman says they are continuing to conduct more missile attacks deep inside Saudi Arabia.”

“As cross-border attacks grow, Yemenis fear the war is coming closer to home, especially as both sides threaten to escalate their attacks, while Saudi Arabia steps up its air campaign,” Mawry added.

Meanwhile, Yemen’s Saudi-backed coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said on Tuesday that its forces have destroyed 127 Houthi weapons depots and missile launch platforms.

Separately, the United Kingdom said it would deploy Royal Air Force jets ⁠on defensive missions to help protect Saudi Arabia from increasing Houthi ⁠attacks.

The British Ministry of Defence said in a statement that the Typhoon warplanes would operate in a “defensive role” and not carry out attacks against the Houthis.

Tensions have soared in Yemen since July, when the Houthis announced a blockade of Saudi ports, and fighting escalated sharply last month when they seized strategic territory from forces loyal to the government along the Red Sea coast.

Government forces, backed by Saudi Arabia, responded to the losses with a counteroffensive and launched Operation Dawn of Yemen, which aims to recapture Houthi-held territory, including Sanaa, seized by the group in 2014.
news.content: یونیسف می گوید تشدید جنگ در تعز سیستم های آبی آن را تهدید می کند و به حدود سه میلیون نفر خدمت رسانی می کند. آژانس پناهندگان سازمان ملل متحد (UNHCR) اعلام کرد که بیش از 250000 نفر در داخل یمن از زمان شروع مجدد جنگ این کشور در ماه ژوئیه آواره داخلی شده اند، زیرا درگیری ها بین شورشیان حوثی و چندین جبهه بین المللی به رسمیت شناخته شده است. کمیساریای عالی پناهندگان سازمان ملل (UNHCR) در بیانیه ای در روز سه شنبه اعلام کرد، شهر تعز در جنوب غربی یمن در مرکز بحران آوارگان قرار دارد و 76 درصد از مهاجران را به خود اختصاص داده و میزبان 52 درصد از آوارگان جدید است. لاهیج در جنوب غربی یمن میزبان 23 درصد از جمعیت تازه آوارگان است، پس از آن عدن در جنوب با 13 درصد از آوارگان سازمان ملل است. این آژانس در بیانیه ای اعلام کرد: «گلوله باران در تعز، از جمله در مناطق مسکونی و اطراف تأسیسات بهداشتی تشدید شد، در حالی که ناامنی و محدودیت ها در مسیرهای کلیدی همچنان دسترسی و حرکت بشردوستانه را محدود می کند». حوثی‌ها، گروهی مسلح که با نام انصارالله (عربی برای حامیان خدا) نیز شناخته می‌شوند، از اوایل اکتبر تعز را محاصره کرده‌اند و جاده‌ای را که آن را به عدن، پایتخت موقت دولت بین‌المللی به رسمیت شناخته‌شده مورد حمایت عربستان سعودی متصل می‌کند، مسدود کرده‌اند. کنفرانس خبری در ژنو، سوئیس. این آژانس گفت که حدود 33700 خانواده هنوز به سرپناه نیاز دارند

اسماعیل بقایی، سخنگوی وزارت خارجه ایران، گفت: «مهم‌ترین مصوبه شورای وزیران سازمان همکاری اسلامی در نشست بغداد، بیانیه پایانی است که معمولا با اجماع تصویب می‌شود. آنچه حدود یکی دو ساعت پیش از تصویب بیانیه مطرح شد، این بود که نباید مواردی در متن بیانیه درج شود که موجب تفرقه میان کشورهای اسلامی شود. مشخصا منظور، موضوع یمن بود.»

یکی از قطعنامه‌های صادر شده در این نشست از ایران خواسته است که «به قواعد حقوق بین‌الملل، منشور ملل متحد و کنوانسیون‌های وین درباره روابط دیپلماتیک و کنسولی احترام بگذارد و با نماینده شبه‌نظامیان حوثی در تهران تعامل نکند.»

بند دیگری از این قطعنامه «از همه کشورها می‌خواهد که با نماینده شبه‌نظامیان حوثی در تهران تعامل نکنند، هیچ‌گونه مکاتبه یا معامله‌ای را از جانب او نپذیرند» چون «چنین مکاتبات و معاملاتی باطل و فاقد هرگونه اثر حقوقی هستند.»

این قطعنامه از دولت‌های عضو سازمان همکاری اسلامی خواسته است از تسهیل سفر نماینده حوثی‌ها در تهران خودداری کنند و «در صورت حضور در قلمروشان، او را به دولت جمهوری یمن تحویل دهند.»

ایران از حوثی‌های یمن که در حال مبارزه با ائتلاف به رهبری عربستان سعودی هستند حمایت می‌کند.

نشست وزیران خارجه این سازمان از ۲۵ مهر به مدت دو روز در پایتخت عراق برگزار شد و از ایران عباس عراقچی در آن شرکت کرد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

وزیر خارجه ایران زمانی که برای اجلاس در بغداد بود گفته بود که اگر در بیانیه نهایی اجلاس «انصاف و توازن» رعایت نشود ممکن است ایران آن را قبول نکند.

او پیش‌بینی کرده بود که «تقریبا اکثر قریب به اتفاق قطعنامه‌ها تکرار سال گذشته» باشد اما در مورد یمن «بحث‌های جدی صورت گرفت. سعودی‌ها نظرات خودشان را داشتند، ما هم نظراتمان را بیان کردیم. کشورهای دیگر هم به همین ترتیب.»

آقای عراقچی همچنین گفت که «بلوک کشورهای نزدیک به مواضع عربستان» در سازمان همکاری اسلامی «قابل توجه» است و «این واقعیتی است که باید در نظر داشته باشیم.»

او گفت که ایران «لابی‌های گسترده‌ای» انجام داده است و اظهار امیدواری کرد که در بیانیه نهایی اجلاس «انصاف و توازن» رعایت شود، در غیر این صورت «جمهوری اسلامی ایران نمی‌تواند به آنها بپیوندد و حتما خودش را از قطعنامه‌های صادره یا آن قطعنامه خاص جدا خواهد کرد، تحفظ [پرهیز] خواهیم کرد. حتی ممکن است که صراحتا اعلام کنیم که قبول نداریم.»

این پنجاه‌ودومین نشست شورای وزیران امور خارجه کشورهای عضو سازمان همکاری‌های اسلامی بود که در سایه جنگ و تنش در منطقه برگزار شد.
